transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I think my eating’s gotten out of hand. It started as me trying to eat cleaner for the lieutenant track, but now I’m cutting meals way down—like black coffee, a protein shake, and maybe a small dinner. Even on shift days, when I know I’ve burned a lot more than that, I’m still doing it.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah. I don’t like admitting it, but yeah. If the scale is up even a pound—like after a big station meal or just drinking extra water—I get this tight panic feeling, like I’ve blown it. I start thinking people are going to see me as soft or like I’ve got no control.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?
Not really. I mean, I’ve had meals where I felt like I ate more than I wanted to, but I don’t think I’ve had those times where I’m eating a huge amount and can’t stop.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up or take laxatives after I eat. That’s not something I’ve been doing.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started cutting down your meals?

Yeah, I have. My gear and station clothes are definitely hanging looser now. They even flagged my weight as too low for my build at the fitness review, but… part of me still feels like I should trim down a little more.
Do you feel like you've lost control while eating at any point?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt guilty after eating more than I planned, but I wouldn’t say I felt out of control or like I couldn’t stop.
Do you think you are currently underweight?

I mean… they told me at the fitness review that my weight was too low for my build, so I guess objectively, yeah. But in my head it doesn’t really feel that way. My gear’s looser, my clothes hang more, but part of me still thinks I could trim down a little more.
Do you think being at a lower weight will improve your performance as a lieutenant?

Yeah… I think I connect it that way. Before work, if I look in the mirror and my waist or my face doesn’t look sharp enough, it gets in my head. I feel less confident, less like I’m ready to be in command. So part of me thinks being lower weight makes me look more prepared, even if I know that may not really be the same as performing better.
Do you think your weight is connected to how you see yourself as a person?

Yeah, I think it is. Like before work, I’ll look in the mirror and focus on whether my waist or my face looks sharp enough. If it doesn’t, it kind of throws me off. I feel less confident, like I’m not as ready to be in charge that day.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is mainly because of how it might affect your performance or appearance as a lieutenant?

Yeah, mostly. It’s not just the number itself—it’s what I think it means. If the scale is up even a pound after a big station meal or just drinking more water, I get this tight panic feeling, like I’ve messed up. Like people are going to look at me and think I’m soft or I don’t have control.
Do you worry about gaining weight because it would change how you see yourself as a person, outside of your role as a lieutenant?

Yeah… I think it does, at least some. Even outside the job, when I look in the mirror, I get stuck on whether my waist or my face looks sharp enough. If they don’t, I don’t feel like myself, or I feel less confident. At work it turns into feeling less command-ready, but it’s also just how I judge myself that day.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how your body looks, rather than just your performance or being seen as soft by others?

Yeah, mostly it’s about how it looks and what I think it says about me. Like if the scale is up even a pound after a big station meal or drinking extra water, I get this tight panic, like I’ve blown it. Then I start thinking people are going to see me as soft or out of control.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the main thing that determines how attractive or unattractive you are to others?

Yeah, I think it plays a big part. Like before work, if I look in the mirror and my waist or my face doesn’t look sharp enough, it really affects how I feel about myself. I feel less confident, and honestly less ready to be in charge that day.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if nobody else could see your body?

Yeah… I think I would. Other people seeing it makes it worse, but even if nobody could, the scale going up—even just a pound after a big meal or extra water—still hits me hard. I get this panic like I messed up or lost control.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you want to maintain a specific body shape?

Yeah. It’s definitely tied to keeping a certain shape. I get caught up in whether my waist and face look sharp enough, especially when I’m looking in the mirror before work. If they don’t, it throws off my confidence and makes me feel less ready to lead that day.
Is your desire to maintain your current weight mostly about looking a certain way?

Yeah, mostly. It’s about how I look to myself—like before work, I’ll check the mirror and focus on whether my waist and face look sharp enough. If they don’t, it really messes with my confidence and how ready I feel to be in charge that day.
Do you think your weight or body shape is distorted when you look in the mirror, even if others might not see it that way?

Yeah, I think so. Like before work, I’ll look in the mirror and get stuck on whether my waist or my face looks sharp enough. If it doesn’t look right to me, even if someone else wouldn’t notice, it can really mess with my confidence and make me feel less ready to be in charge that day.
Do you think you would see yourself as overweight even if a doctor told you your weight is normal?

Yeah, I think I probably would. Even if a doctor said my weight was normal, when I look in the mirror before work I still focus on whether my waist and face look sharp enough. If they don’t look right to me, it really affects how confident and ready I feel that day.
Do you think your body looks a certain way that doesn't match how others see you?

Yeah. I think what I see is probably different from what other people see. Like, I’ll check the mirror before work and get really focused on whether my waist or my face looks sharp enough. If it doesn’t look that way to me, it throws off my confidence and I don’t feel as ready to be in command that day.
Do you think you would still see yourself as overweight even if you were at a healthy weight according to medical standards?

Yeah, I think I would. Even if I was told my weight was healthy, I’d still probably look in the mirror before work and focus on whether my waist and face look sharp enough. If they don’t look right to me, it messes with my confidence and whether I feel ready to take command that day.
